head: i

dp[i]
rows: `love` (4) then rest: (12 - 4)² + 0; `love leetcode` is 13, too wide

head: Code
Meaning
Reach for it when
rows: The number of rounds person k needs
Someone in front of (or equal to) k buys once per round, up to their own need
Someone behind k has bought one fewer time when k finishes
Total seconds = total tickets bought by everyone until k is done

p: Total `6`. For `tickets = [5,1,1,1]`, `k = 0`: person 0 contributes 5, each of the others `min(1, 4) = 1`, total `8`.

2073.takeaway: Count how many tickets each person buys before person k finishes: people up to and including k buy at most tickets[k], people after k buy at most tickets[k] - 1.

head: Code

Remove from the front until `j` is gone (this removes `i` too)
Remove from the back until `i` is gone
Remove the front part through `i` and the back part from `j`

p: `nums = [2,10,7,5,4,1,8,6]`: the maximum `10` is at index 1, the minimum `1` at index 5, so `i = 1`, `j = 5`, `n = 8`.

2091.takeaway: Only the positions of the minimum and maximum matter; try the three ways to clear both: from the front, from the back, or one from each end.

2124.takeaway: Every 'a' comes before every 'b' exactly when the string never contains "ba".

head: Code
Meaning
Reach for it when
rows: Every third candy (positions 2, 5, 8, ...) is the free one
Taking the grouping out of the sorted order
Add up the candies that are paid for

p: Why it is right: the free candy must cost no more than the cheaper of the two paid ones, so grouping neighbours in sorted order wastes the least.

bullets: Space: O(n) for the sorted copy.

2144.takeaway: Sort the prices from the highest down; in each group of three, pay for the two most expensive and take the cheapest free.

2170.takeaway: The even-index and odd-index positions are independent: keep the most common value on each side, unless they are the same value, in which case use the second best on one side.

head: Code
Meaning
Reach for it when
rows: `(first char, last char, longest run starting at the left edge, longest run ending at the right edge, longest run anywhere, length)`
If the last char of `a` equals the first of `b`, the runs join: best also considers `a.suffix + b.prefix`, and prefix/suffix grow when a half is a single run
Leaves are stored from index `size`, parents at `i // 2`
A single character: all run lengths are 1
Recompute every ancestor of the changed leaf, O(log n)
The root's best run is the longest run of the whole string

p: `s = "babacc"`, queries set index 1 to `b`, index 3 to `c`, then index 3 to `b`.

bullets: Time: O(n + q log n) for n characters and q queries.

2213.takeaway: A segment tree where each node stores (left char, right char, prefix run, suffix run, best run, length); merging two halves joins runs that touch, and each update only redoes the nodes above one leaf.

head: Code
Meaning
Reach for it when
rows: Among equal distances, a larger `x` gives a smaller `-x`, so the positive one wins
Picks the element with the smallest key tuple
Selecting by a computed key without sorting

p: The smallest key is `(1, -1)`, so the answer is `1`. For `[2,-1,1]` the keys `(1, 1)` for -1 and `(1, -1)` for 1 tie on distance, and `(1, -1)` wins, giving `1`.

2239.takeaway: Take the minimum of the numbers by the key (absolute value, then larger value first) so ties go to the positive number.

head: Code
Meaning

Following a functional graph (one outgoing edge per node)
Guard against looping around a cycle forever
Nodes reachable from both start nodes
The later of the two arrivals; we want this as small as possible
Minimising the worse of two quantities

p: Common nodes: `2` with `max(1, 1) = 1` and `3` with `max(2, 2) = 2`. The best is node `2`.

2359.takeaway: Walk from each start node along the single outgoing edges to record distances, then among nodes reachable from both pick the one with the smallest maximum distance.

head: Code
Meaning
Reach for it when
rows: Counter of the values in the current subset; missing values read as 0
Number of valid ways to finish from index i (counting the empty choice as one way)
No chosen value differs from `x` by exactly k
The empty subset was counted, but the problem wants non-empty ones

p: That is 5 subsets including the empty one, so the answer is `5 - 1 = 4`.

2597.takeaway: Backtracking over include/exclude choices, with a Counter of chosen values so a number can be added only when neither x - k nor x + k is already chosen.

p: Why it is right: choosing an index with a left and a right copy deletes both, so the count of a letter drops by 2 (or by 1 at the edge); one copy always survives, and each letter can be cut down to a single copy.

2716.takeaway: The operation can remove every duplicate but never the last copy of a letter, so the minimum length is the number of distinct letters.
